# task-ad7a9b54 — 1-panel anti-diagonal reflection

## Confirmed rule
The grid is mostly 0. Find the rectangular region filled with color 1 (which may contain other colors). Ignore the surrounding 0 field and any isolated colored noise outside the rectangle. Copy the entire rectangle—including its 1 background and all embedded non-1 cells—and reflect it across its anti-diagonal (top-right to bottom-left). The output dimensions are swapped: an H×W panel becomes W×H.

Coordinate rule for panel-local source coordinate `(r,c)` using zero-based indexing:

`output[W - 1 - c][H - 1 - r] = panel[r][c]`

Equivalently, output cell `(i,j)` is `panel[H - 1 - j][W - 1 - i]`. Do not use an ordinary clockwise or counterclockwise rotation; this is anti-diagonal reflection.

## Evidence
Demo 1: extracted 9×10 panel from the 23×19 grid (rows 1–9, cols 2–11, zero-based). The embedded 8-pattern and 2/4 cells all mapped exactly under anti-diagonal reflection to the 10×9 output. Exterior singletons (colors 3, 4, 2) were not copied.

## Pitfalls / validation
- Identify the full bounding rectangle of the 1 region, not just the non-1 motif.
- Include all embedded colors, including isolated values inside the rectangle.
- Exclude external markers and 0 padding.
- Carefully track zero-based rectangle bounds and verify output has W rows, each H cells.
